verdict.rationale: Community users describe Framer as strong for advanced prototyping with animations and transitions, and first-party docs say the AI agent wires interactive elements such as animated menus and carousels from a description, with no code. There are no first-party docs on linking screens into clickable flows, defining triggers, configuring transitions, or using overlays, and the prototyping comments refer to an older Framer X era. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of screen-to-screen linking, interaction triggers, transition settings, overlays, and recent hands-on corroboration of no-code prototyping.

support.subject: As a designer, I can wire screens into clickable prototypes with triggers, transitions, and overlays — no code required

citations.quote: Framer is great for more advanced prototyping needs w/ animations/transitions/etc
Sticky navbars, animated menus, interactive carousels, just describe what you want. The agent handles the wiring so you can focus on the design, not the how-to.
Your prototypes can use actual data
